sentences.text: Heard the learned counsels for the parties.

sentences.text: The learned counsel for the petitioner in BA No. 2598 of 2024 submits that it is alleged that from the possession of this petitioner four mobile phones with three SIM Cards were seized and one SIM was found to be issued in fake name.
It is further submitted that the petitioner is a driver and never involved in any cyber crime.
It is further stated that petitioner has got criminal antecedent.
The learned APP has opposed the bail application and submitted that lot of transactions have been found from the mobile phones and SIM recovered from the petitioner.
The learned counsel for the petitioner in BA No. 2681 of 2024 submits that it is alleged that one mobile phone was seized from this petitioner.
It is further submitted that not a single individual has come forward with an allegation that the petitioner has cheated them.
It is further stated that petitioner has got no criminal antecedent.
The learned counsel for the State, learned APP has opposed the bail application and submitted that one mobile phone was seized from the petitioner and the petitioner has confessed his guilt.

The learned counsel for the petitioner in BA No. 2834 of 2024 submits that it is alleged that the petitioner was apprehended from his house and some mobile phones, ATM Cards, Pass Books,
Cheque Books, Pan Cards, Aadhar Cards, Bajaj Pulsar motorcycle, 10 SIM Cards and a cash of Rs.
8,29,600/- was recovered but most of the recoveries are planted as apart from one or two SIM Cards, none of the SIMs were issued in the name of the petitioner and the recovery of ATM and Debit Cards were issued in the name of the petitioner, his father and other family members and retaining more than one ATM Card or Debit Card by a single name is not an offence.
Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that amount of Rs. 8,29,600/- was a sale proceed of land sold by father of petitioner and the said amount cannot be projected as crime money.
It is further submitted that the petitioner has got no criminal antecedent.

The learned counsel for the State has opposed the bail application and submitted that from the house of the petitioner some mobile phones, ATM Cards, Pass Books, Cheque Books, Pan Cards,
Aadhar Cards, Bajaj Pulsar motorcycle and 10 SIM Cards and a cash of Rs. 8,29,600/- was recovered.

The learned counsel for the petitioner in BA No. 2909 of 2024 submits that it is alleged that two mobile phones were recovered from the possession of this petitioner but the mobile phones which were recovered from the possession of this petitioner are his own mobile phones.
It is further submitted that petitioner has got no criminal antecedent.
Learned counsel for the State, has opposed the bail petition and submitted that two mobile phones were recovered from the possession of this petitioner.
The learned counsels for all the petitioners have stated that all the petitioners are in custody from 10.12.2023.

2 Having heard both counsels, gone through the records of the case and in the facts and circumstances of the case, I am inclined to release the petitioners of all the bail applications, named above, on bail,
on furnishing bail bond of Rs. 25,000/- (rupees twenty five thousand only) each with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned Additional Sessions Judge-II- cum- Special Judge ( Cyber Crime) Giridih in connection with Giridih ( Cyber) P.S. Case No. 38 of 2023, subject to the condition that the petitioners shall report to the concerned police station on every last Saturday of the month, between 01:00 and 05:00 p.m for one year, failing which or if any adverse remarks regarding their non-appearance at the police station, their bail bonds shall be liable to be cancelled.

Any exemption to such attendance shall be done so after direction of the learned Court below and the petitioners shall remain present on each and every date of trial before the Court below unless dispensed with by the learned Court below with further condition that the petitioners will submit their mobile numbers before the learned court below which they will always keep active and will not change it during pendency of this case without prior permission of the court.

(Ratnaker Bhengra, J.) Sharda/
